The text highlights the transformative potential of quantum computing, specifically noting its impact on cryptography and drug discovery through the unique properties of qubits. In the context of database systems, this relates to the field of post-quantum cryptography, where database administrators and security engineers are actively researching and implementing new encryption standards to protect stored data against future quantum attacks. Furthermore, the mention of modeling complex molecular structures connects to bioinformatics databases, which store vast amounts of genomic and proteomic data. Quantum computing could significantly accelerate the processing and analysis of these large-scale datasets, enabling faster identification of drug candidates and a deeper understanding of biological systems stored within these repositories.

A group of crows is called a murder.
